title: Illness Early-Warning Composite
dataSources: HRV (`hrv:reading`), blood oxygen (`spo2:reading`), lab panels (`bloodpanel:result`), supplements (`supplement:intake`), continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), sleep-apnea events (`apnea:event`), body composition (`bodycomp:measure`).
app: Biohacking and advanced-health data — HRV chest straps, pulse oximeters, blood-pressure cuffs, continuous glucose monitors, body-composition scales, lab-result exports, and supplement logs — ingested to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=hrv:reading OR sourcetype=whoop:cycle OR sourcetype=oura:daily)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(rmssd_ms) as hrv, avg(resting_hr) as rhr, avg(skin_temp_dev_c) as temp_dev by _time
| eventstats avg(hrv) as hrv_base, avg(rhr) as rhr_base
| eval warning=if(hrv<hrv_base*0.8 AND rhr>rhr_base+3 AND temp_dev>0.3,1,0)
description: Combines a dropping HRV, rising resting heart rate, and raised skin temperature into a single you-might-be-getting-sick signal.
value: These three signs shift a day or two before symptoms; combining them catches an oncoming illness while rest can still help.
implementation: Ingest recovery metrics into `index=personal`; schedule daily and alert when all three point the wrong way at once.
visualization: Multi-metric panel with a combined illness-warning flag.
grandmaExplanation: It combines several body signals that change before you feel ill, giving you a heads-up to rest before a cold takes hold.
